properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 28 at 10:45AM AST until October 28 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North facing beaches of Puerto Rico, including Culebra.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 6 PM AST THIS EVENING

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 28 at 10:38AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS
EVENING TO 10 AM EDT THURSDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 28 at 5:49AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Low temperatures in the upper teens Wednesday morning has caused
the 4-7 inches of wet snow from Monday, that had partially melted
Tuesday, to refreeze. Slick surfaces are expected across the
Fairbanks Metro Area as wet surfaces and small water puddles have
frozen into thin sheets of ice. Areas of heavy, wet snow have also
frozen into a sturdier, more ice like form. Travel may be
impacted, especially during the Wednesday morning commute.

Additional rain and snow showers are expected overnight Wednesday
into Thursday with much lighter accumulations than Monday. Less
than an inch of new snow is possible with only a few hundredths of
an inch of liquid equivalent expected.

properties.description:
A trough moving over the state is bringing abundant tropical
moisture expected to last though this evening. Heavy rain and
isolated thunderstorms are expected to produce flash flooding, and
while the greatest flood threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui
County, all islands are at risk.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...All main Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

may develop at any time through tonight as a trough continues
moving over the state. While the greatest flood threat will be
focused over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are at risk.

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 28 at 3:46AM AKDT until October 28 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the normal highest
tide line.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT today, highest water levels expected
during each upcoming high tide through this morning.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady south to southwesterly flow is
expected to continue for the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through
this morning. Coastal erosion and perhaps nuisance flooding of
low-lying areas will be possible with high tide due to the
persistent onshore winds. Possible maximum water levels of
between 1 and 2 ft above the normal highest tide line, including
in and around Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. A brief break in winds
and thus, elevated water levels occurs late today, but a second
round of elevated water levels and persistent southerly winds
are forecast with the arrival of yet another front late Thursday
into Friday.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.description:

flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected.

evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

rip currents.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 28 at 2:40AM EDT until October 30 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11
feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Friday
night. For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 AM EDT Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
Typhoon In-fa is expected to pass through the far northern CNMI
somewhere between Sarigan and Maug sometime on Friday.
Winds and seas will increase late Thursday ahead of the
approaching typhoon, quickly exceeding hazardous levels to small
craft by early Friday morning, with seas peaking at 11 to 14 feet
for Tinian and Saipan, and 8 to 12 feet for Guam and Rota.
Mariners are urged to take precautions and remain weather aware
over the coming days.

properties.areaDesc: Rio Arriba, NM; Taos, NM
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 27 at 7:44PM MDT until October 30 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Rio Grande at Embudo affecting Rio Arriba and Taos Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Embudo.

* WHEN...From this evening to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Minor overbank flows are occurring above the
Embudo gaging site. Access to riverside picnic facilities above
Pilar and below the Taos Junction Bridge along State Route 570 will
be limited if further rises occur. Water may be extremely close to
underside of bridge over Rio Grande on Aguas Caliente Rd in Pilar.
Other localized effects due to the high water levels will begin to
be felt at a stage of 10 feet but no significant flooding is
expected until the river rises to 12 feet.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:00 PM MDT Tuesday the stage was 7.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.4 feet
early Thursday morning.
- Action stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at noon MDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM THIS EVENING TO FRIDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Socorro, NM
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 6:54PM MDT until October 29 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, streets in the village of San Francisco
between interstate 25 and the Rio Grande just south of Bernardo are
being flooded. Water levels in the Lower Rio Puerco have not been
this high since July of 1944. The nearby railroad bridge may also
be flooded. Further rises will impact Interstate 25 traffic.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 PM MDT Tuesday the stage was 19.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
evening to a crest of 21.8 feet Wednesday morning. It will then
fall below flood stage Thursday.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 27 at 3:36PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend. 1-3 more inches of precipitation
are expected by the end of the week which will keep water levels
high.

No flooding is expected at this time, however residents living near
local rivers and streams should be vigilant of the potential for ice
in culverts and other stream passage structures to restrict flow
resulting water flowing over roads in affected areas.

properties.areaDesc: Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 27 at 2:20PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Between 4 and 7 inches of heavy, wet, snow fell across the
Fairbanks Metro Area Monday. Warming temperatures Monday evening
into Tuesday have caused portions of that snowfall to melt,
creating many slushy areas of melting snow and pooling water.
Overnight low temperatures Tuesday night into Wednesday morning
are expected to fall into the upper teens to low 20s which will
allow much of this slush to refreeze. Slick surfaces are very
likely Wednesday morning as wet surfaces and small water puddles
freeze. Areas of heavy, wet snow will also refreeze giving the
slush a sturdier, more ice like texture. Travel may be impacted,
especially during the Wednesday morning commute.

Additional rain and snow showers are expected overnight Wednesday
into Thursday with much lighter accumulations than Monday. Less
than an inch of new snow is possible with only a few hundredths of
an inch of liquid equivalent expected.

* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be through
Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal Flood
Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf develops.
The Coastal Flood Advisory may also need to be extended beyond
Thursday.
properties.instruction:

NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.
